- 92 real shell outputs from other people's agent runs join the corpus, so the benchmark is not only cases written to find gaps. Source: [nvidia/SWE-Hero-openhands-trajectories](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/SWE-Hero-openhands-trajectories), CC BY 4.0, tasks from MIT, Apache-2.0 and BSD repositories only (41 MIT, 25 BSD-3, 23 Apache-2.0, 3 BSD-2). `benchmark/ATTRIBUTION.md` credits each case and states that these files stay under their own licences, not the repo's MIT.
- `scripts/quality-public.ts` draws them by rules fixed before any scoring. It takes 100 trajectories at even offsets, and from each the first `execute_bash` output of 4,096 to 30,000 characters that holds a fact and no secret, with OpenHands' trailer lines removed. The dataset revision is pinned, and files are replaced only once every row is fetched.
- PR 3 of 5 for #390 tier 1. SWE-Hero was chosen over SWE-smith (SWE-agent's own file viewer, not raw shell; upstream licences not filtered) and SWE-rebench (no per-row licence).

Part of #390.

## What it shows

The sample is what SWE agents run: 66 pytest, 14 grep, 8 python, 3 other, 1 git diff.

| Family | Cases (compressed) | mcp-recall | Head, same size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pytest | 68 (58) | 75.8% | 17.4% |
| grep | 15 (7) | 74.1% | 56.1% |
| python | 8 (8) | 69.3% | 42.6% |
| git-diff | 3 (2) | 44.8% | 46.4% |

(Families mix scripted and public cases. A case mcp-recall passes through scores 100% in both columns.)

## Found along the way (filed separately)

- #401, fixed in #402: Claude Code 2.1.305 adds a line count to the saved-result notice, which the unreleased #393 reader missed.
- #403: the JSON fallback elides every value below depth 3, so an MCP envelope keeps only its keys. It hit both Hugging Face reads in this session.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test`: 1376 pass; `bun run typecheck` clean; `--check` passes in a clean env
- [x] Sampler run twice: byte-identical cases. A run cut off by HTTP 429 used to leave the corpus half-deleted; it now writes only after every row is fetched (rerun after the fix: cases unchanged)
- [x] 12 mutations of the sampler's rules each turn a test red, each confirmed applied
- [x] No secrets (mcp-recall's scanner over every case) and no machine paths in the corpus; `npm pack --dry-run` ships nothing from `benchmark/`
